open.review: FALSIFIED IN ITS REASONING, HELD IN ITS CONCLUSION - 16 Sep 04:30Z. Yesterday's entry said 'ESPN flags him QUESTIONABLE and no injury appears in any reporting retrieved today - treat the tag as stale, which is a judgement and not a clearance.' That judgement was wrong and the honesty of labelling it as a judgement is the only thing that saved it. RotoWire, retrieved tonight: Mason is nursing thumb soreness from the Vikings-Packers opener, is a day-to-day concern and is 'being further evaluated', with Kevin O'Connell saying the team awaits test results before clarifying his Week 2 status. The same report supplies the usage detail the earlier entry lacked - 30 of 65 offensive snaps, 15 carries, 59 yards, one touchdown and ZERO TARGETS, with Aaron Jones at 29 snaps. Zero targets in full PPR is the profile STRATEGY section 2 calls uniquely bad. Separately, Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and Carson Wentz is expected to start against Chicago, which points Minnesota's plan further toward the run and is the only thing that cuts in Mason's favour. The decline stands, now on evidence rather than on a judgement, and it is published in whatWentWrong rather than quietly corrected. LESSON FOR FUTURE RUNS: 'no injury reporting was retrieved' is not the same as 'no injury exists'; search the player's own news feed, not only his weekly-outlook coverage.
